@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Introduction：

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · dsh-TUI：> An interactive terminal UI for DeepSeek Harness. It ships a pixel-whale
> header, live work status, streaming thinking, double-Esc time rewind, a
> context progress bar, and a TPS gauge. Zero core changes: it consumes only
> DSH's public exports, and is moving from a mounted plugin to an app with its
> own entry and composition root, where DSH loads in process as the first-party
> backend. Install to enable; uninstall leaves no patches behind.
The prompt footer hides completed goals once the turn is idle; the Todo side panel retains their history. `Ctrl+Q` folds todos while working and hides/restores the idle goal/todo footer. Clicking its todo header also hides it while idle. Hiding changes only this display: a new goal/todo snapshot or session reveals it again, and `/goal clear` does not clear todos.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · dsh-TUI：Split diff cards give one-sided additions and deletions the full body width, without an empty opposite pane. Ordinary edits remain side by side, and mixed files choose their layout separately before folding or streaming reveal.

Compaction status stays on one line in narrow panes: phase and cancellation hints yield first, then the label is shortened; elapsed time is shown only as a complete field.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · dsh-TUI：Image files referenced with `@path` use the same admission and resize/conversion policy as pasted images. Adjustment notices report the stored dimensions and format; required animation conversion is refused instead of dropping frames. Mention images and staged images still share count and stored-byte limits in source order.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Highlights：Panels without a verified Component identity are temporary: settings show their title and a distinct number for this run. Their toggles take effect immediately without being saved, and unrelated settings changes preserve that choice. Old `actN:panel` entries cannot be mapped safely: remove the placeholder and select the current panel again. Verified Components named `actN` keep their public runtime address; an explicit selection uses `component:actN:panel` in saved preferences to avoid claiming an old anonymous entry.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Highlights：The default reasoning-effort setting offers the current backend/model’s declared tiers, including custom IDs. Saved values absent from that catalog stay visible and stored; while loading or unavailable, only Auto is selectable. On DSH, Auto follows the saved `/effort` choice, then the configured effort, then the model default. Claude/Codex retain backend preferences for Auto at startup and for resumed sessions; explicitly choosing Auto resets the model default. Explicit settings changes affect the next request; unsupported preferences fall back with a notice and are never forced onto a route.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Highlights：Resuming a DSH session preserves its recorded reasoning effort (or its live selection when reattaching). The saved default seeds new sessions; explicit `/effort` and effort-default settings changes still apply to the current session’s next request.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Highlights：- **Pixel whale pet** — three startup intros, click to wake; freezes after the first task.
- **Launchpad and first-run guide** — every ordinary launch lands on a landing page with a **real input box** (big text + whale + quick actions, dropping whole blocks on short/narrow terminals; whale-girl images use a compact native-canvas footprint instead of leaving a large gap before the title; on by default — /settings `launchpad` off boots straight into chat); command completion matches chat: `Tab` fills the input, `Enter` runs the command and clears it. The first run walks a four-step wizard (accounts & models / language+theme / model+workspace / shortcuts), re-runnable with `/setup`; its first step signs in to a subscription and catches the models it brings in (none → no question, one → that one, several → you choose), or adds an API key through the `/provider` wizard, which asks which of the enabled models to switch to or keeps the current one.
- **Terminal-native UI** — streaming Markdown, tool cards, `/` and `@` completion, `#L12-14` ranges, history search, zh/en UI.
- **Task completion notifications** — DSH, Claude and Codex notify

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Highlights：Keys and commands: [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md). Everything else: [documentation index](docs/README.md).

Plugin side panels stay enabled when unrelated settings change. Editing the enabled panel list still applies your explicit selection.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Highlights：Workspace side-panel counts match the session manager: the current conversation counts; empty logs, subagents, fork ancestors and archived sessions do not. Registered workspaces with no visible conversations remain at zero. Loading and read errors are shown separately; press `r` to refresh.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Highlights：When a DSH 0.2.1+ Agent moves its session to another directory (the `working_directory` tool or a Git worktree), the status line, Git branch, `@` completion, `!` commands, clicked paths, skill commands and loaded context follow it, including after `/resume`. The session stays registered under the project it started in. Relative paths in cards rendered before a move resolve against the session's current directory when clicked; absolute paths keep their target.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Highlights：Fullscreen mouse selection stays in the pane where the gesture starts, including chat, sidebar and either diff column. Diagonal, word and line selection copy that pane’s text; soft wraps join independently, source newlines remain, and divider drags only resize.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Both `dsh-tui` and the short `dst` alias start the same TUI.：> **New-user note**: pnpm ≥11 blocks dependencies with install scripts by
> default and reports `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`. Updates skip foreign-platform
> natives — the `@img/sharp-*` packages and the Claude SDK's per-platform
> bundles — so only this machine's binaries are fetched. `/update` and
> `dsh-tui update` write both settings automatically. An update never installs
> the Claude SDK on its own: it enters a profile only when you pick that
> backend in the kernel picker, which then installs the pinned SDK for the
> running platform. No manual step needed. Details:

text:
@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Both `dsh-tui` and the short `dst` alias start the same TUI.：After startup the TUI checks for newer versions in the background. It never
blocks the first frame. Type `/update` for a one-shot upgrade of the whole set
— TUI, dsh engine and global launcher. It restarts automatically and resumes
the current session, and refuses instead of leaving an incompatible or
unbootable TUI/engine combination. Launcher alignment is normally best effort,
but a failure after the engine advances blocks the restart and prints a repair
command. If the registry has a newer dsh release outside the TUI's
validated line, it says so and waits for a TUI update rather than installing an
unvalidated engine. Launcher alignment only touches proven global installs;
local npm/npx packages, ambiguous aliases and multi-member pnpm groups stay
unchanged. See
[Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md) for the profile lifecycle,
source builds, and troubleshooting, including migration from the former
`dsh-cc-tui` package.
section: Both `dsh-tui` and the short `dst` alias start the same TUI.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · CLI：| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh-tui` / `dst` | Start the TUI; `dst` is a short alias for the same program |
| `dsh-tui --resume [id]` · `dsh-tui update` · `dsh-tui doctor` | Resume a session · align the TUI, dsh engine and global launcher as one set · pre-flight environment checks |
| `dsh-tui safe` | Read-only diagnostics, plugin inventory and repair guidance; `safe --rescue` builds a clean rescue profile |
| `dsh-tui version` · `dsh-tui help` | Launcher and profile versions and usage; both work even without a `dsh` install |

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · CLI：Leading DSH options such as `--dump-config` and `--patch <path>` are forwarded
unchanged; other arguments go to the app in `dsh --profile dsh-tui`. Use
`dsh-tui -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes` to send `--resume=sid-1 ./notes` as literal
prompt text, without selecting a session or workspace. When invoking DSH
directly, use `dsh --profile dsh-tui -- -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes`: the first
`--` belongs to DSH, the second to the app. Host options can precede a literal
prompt: `dsh-tui --patch ./overlay.yml -- --resume=sid-1` applies the overlay
and sends `--resume=sid-1` as prompt text without resuming that session.
Safe mode: [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md).

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`)：Bring Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversation histories into the DSH session store, then browse and resume them by their original working directory via `/resume`:

```sh
dsh-tui migrate                # list importable counts per agent (writes nothing)
dsh-tui migrate claude-code    # import every Claude Code conversation (likewise codex / omp / zcode / grok-build)
dsh-tui migrate codex --dry-run  # preview what would land, write nothing
```
section: Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`)

text:
@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`)：- **Read-only source**: migration only reads the foreign agent's local store; artifacts are written through the official `JsonlSessionPersistence` backend, so imported sessions are first-class (openable, continuable).
- **Idempotent**: one deterministic UUID per source conversation — re-importing skips what is already present instead of stacking duplicates.
- **Structure preserved**: user/assistant messages, reasoning traces, tool calls with their results, and the source's context compactions (as native compaction checkpoints) are rebuilt turn by turn; harness-injected machine text opens no turn. An imported session can pick the work straight up.
In-TUI browsing: the session screen (`/resume`) shows a tab per agent that has conversations; picking one imports just that conversation and opens it.
In-TUI: `/migrate` (optionally `/migrate <agent> [--dry-run]`) runs the same import in a child process and reports through the notification flow.
CLI alternative: `dsh-tui migrate ...` from any shell runs the same import.
Full guide: [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md).
section: Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`)

text: @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`)：**VS Code**: use the integrated terminal or the `dsh-tui-vscode` extension. See [VS Code guide](docs/vscode.en.md). **Herdr**: run `dsh-tui` in a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane; `idle` / `working` / `blocked` are reported through its local integration API. **Any terminal**: dsh-tui reports `idle` / `working` / `blocked` / `done` / `error` over the pty with [OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status), so terminals and agentic inboxes that implement it can show what the session is doing; terminals that do not implement it ignore the sequence. Set `DSH_TUI_PROGRAM_STATUS=0` to turn it off.

text:
@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`)：Bare `--resume` (`-c`, `--continue`) reopens the last session of the backend this
launch selected. Startup recovery only ever targets that backend: a backend with no
last session, or a derived target that belongs to a different backend than the one
that actually booted (an unknown backend id falling back to DSH, `--backend` naming
a backend that is not installed, a remembered kernel that is not the marker's
source), refuses with a clear error and exit code 1 — never a silent cold start,
never another backend's session, never a new session. An explicit `--resume <id>`
passes that id to the selected backend as-is. The one exception is safe mode's
"retry normal startup": it retries the kernel and session recorded in
`last-run.json`, so a record whose backend is gone degrades to a warning plus a cold
start — that retry is the last way back.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: native Codex backend：Run your own Codex through `codex app-server`, sharing its configuration,
login, instructions, skills, hooks, MCP and native threads:

```sh
npm install -g @openai/codex@0.160.1
dsh-tui --backend codex
dsh-tui --backend codex --resume <thread-id>
```

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: native Codex backend：Protocol baseline **0.160.1**, minimum **0.144.0**; other versions may show
drift. `CODEX_EXECUTABLE` selects a binary; `/kernel` remembers the backend.
`codex resume <id>` can open the same thread after the other writer exits.
This is not `migrate codex`, which imports history into DSH.
With native credentials, a writer conflict for an idle thread retained by the
official background server triggers a reconnection to that server. Managed
subscription credentials and `/channel` connections use private app-server processes.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: native Codex backend：Streaming/tool cards, approvals, questions, steer/queue/interrupt, model and
effort controls, Plan, `/review`, `/diff`, `/usage`, `/init`, skills and MCP
share the existing UI. Async questions open the questionnaire while Codex
continues working; answers steer the turn (or queue if unavailable), and
dismissing the question leaves work running. **Shift+Tab only toggles Plan**, keeping its underlying
permission preset; Full Access requires an explicit choice. Existing Codex
settings are respected, not overwritten with defaults. `/login` offers
ChatGPT OAuth, a device code or an API key (the last writes to Codex’s own
credential store). Relay `/channel` connections take precedence; managed
subscription tokens are only injected on first-party routes. dsh-TUI does
not write `~/.codex/config.toml` or log out your native Codex account. A
provider `env_key` from your own config (e.g. `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) that the
shell did not export is injected from the DSH credential store when the ref
is stored there — the active store first, then the default `~/.dsh` one — so
keep the key in the store, no per-shell export needed.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: native Codex backend：For Claude and Codex, `/channel` tokens (`CHANNEL_*` refs) belong to the
active `DSH_HOME` only. Disconnecting a channel cannot revive a token from
the default home; reconnect it in the active home if needed. Provider
`env_key` credentials retain the fallback described above.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: native Codex backend：TPS includes hidden reasoning time and excludes tool execution time. Live
text estimates are corrected when Codex reports output token usage. Decode
spans of 500ms or less are excluded from TPS samples; token and cost totals
still include all reported usage.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: native Codex backend：Native browsing/archive, fork/conversation rewind (the first message requires
Codex app-server 0.160.1+), paged history, images,
subagents, polled background terminals, goals and `/btw`/`/recap` use the
existing surfaces. `/logout` removes only the matching dsh-auth credential;
already-loaded managed tokens require a normal restart, not native logout.
The real 0.160.1 app-server passed nine credential-free offline checks and eight
daemon-resume checks, with no model turn or charge; real subscription login, credentialed model calls
and real-TTY interaction were not run. Only Codex identification/title
changes automatically, not palette or companion.
Using ChatGPT subscription tokens in third-party clients is subject to
OpenAI’s terms. Full instructions and current boundaries:
[Codex backend](docs/codex-backend.en.md).

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: DSH Agent Teams：DSH's experimental Agent Teams lets the session's agent (the Lead) create
named teammates that share the working directory, message each other and
coordinate on a shared task board. It ships with dsh, is off by default, and
`/plugin list` advertises it. Switch it on:

```sh
/plugin enable @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile
```

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: DSH Agent Teams：The switch enables or disables the bundle in the profile, so it persists
across restarts, and on a `dsh --profile` launch it applies at once — running
sessions included: the model is told which tools came and went. `/team` appears
in Help and `/` completion only once the team service is mounted, and only
reports: `/team` (or `/team status`) shows the bundle, the service and this
session's teammates. `/team on|off` was removed; typing it points at
`/plugin enable|disable`. Turning the bundle off while teammates run asks
first, and switching off stops them: the team service releases the teammates
still running as it unloads. Inside a teammate session the other teammates'
runs are not visible, so the question counts them as possibly running. The
team record stays in the session and comes back when the bundle is enabled
again.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: DSH Agent Teams：If the running DSH does not ship the bundle (`/plugin list` stays silent),
switch DSH to one of the supported lines first (`0.2.2-rc.1`, `0.2.1-rc.5`, `0.2.1-rc.4`, `0.2.1-rc.3`,
`0.2.1-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.5`, `0.2.0-rc.1` or `0.2.0-rc.2`). To install it into the profile explicitly,
run `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile@<your-dsh-version>`:
the team packages ship in lockstep with DSH and pin their DSH peers exactly,
so the version must match.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Experimental: DSH Agent Teams：While a request carries `spawn_teammate`, dsh-TUI drops `subagent` /
`subagent_fork` from it, and the team's `send_message` / `list_agents` /
`interrupt_agent` / `wait_agent` take the place of the legacy controls of the
same names, so `spawn_teammate` is the delegation tool; with the team off
the legacy tools are back. Subagents that are not team members (workflow,
ralph) keep `subagent`. A teammate shows up as a subagent row, a message between
members as a `✉ <sender>` bubble in the receiving session (a teammate's
received messages show on its subagent detail as agent messages), and the
other team tools as one-line cards (`send_message` with its target and
`sent`). The agents dashboard (Ctrl+A) and the agents side
panel switch to a team view: each teammate under its member name with

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：The goal bar stays on one summary line: hovering truncated goal text in fullscreen or split shows the whole objective, and a bare `/goal` prints the full status — objective, phase, rounds or budget, available commands — as a transcript block in the `/plugins` shape. @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：While the model is working: `Enter` steers, `Tab` queues a follow-up, `Ctrl+Enter` interrupts and sends. Input that names a command is still a command — with or without arguments — so `/model` or `/new` reach their own gate (and the `/` overlay sinks the commands that affect the running conversation) instead of silently becoming an interruption; only text that is not a command — and a direct skill gesture such as `/skill-name …` — steers.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：When DSH ends a turn because its session was disposed, the transcript shows “Session stopped”; user interruption keeps its existing prompt for what to do next. This describes the reported stop reason and does not recover a stuck session or its queued inputs.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：Windows Neovim/Vim terminals identified by `NVIM` or `VIM_TERMINAL` retain VT input instead of enabling ConPTY mode 9001. For another incompatible embedded host, set `DSH_TUI_DISABLE_WIN32_INPUT_MODE=1` before launch (PowerShell: `$env:DSH_TUI_DISABLE_WIN32_INPUT_MODE="1"`). The same gate applies at startup and after resume. Native Windows Terminal, conhost and VS Code keep their existing mode unless disabled; the opt-out can remove modified-Enter reporting.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：Extended key reporting (Kitty keyboard protocol and xterm `modifyOtherKeys`) is enabled for a fixed terminal list: iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Ghostty, rio, Orca, tmux, Warp and Windows Terminal. A terminal missing from that list can opt in with `DSH_TUI_FORCE_EXTENDED_KEYS=1`, and `DSH_TUI_DISABLE_EXTENDED_KEYS=1` opts an allowlisted terminal back out for SSH or nested xterm.js hosts (it wins when both are set). Outside native Windows, where win32-input-mode reports Enter's modifiers instead and is not touched by this switch, a terminal without extended keys cannot tell `Shift+Enter` from `Enter`, and `Ctrl+J` is the newline fallback.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：On native Windows, fragmented Win32 input records are reassembled across short input delays instead of appearing as numeric protocol text. The platform check only reports that this machine might run the private mode (win32-input-mode); a bare `ESC[` fragment is held only after one record has actually been decoded, while a fragment whose own shape is already record-specific holds on its own (which is how even the first record can survive a split). Windows terminals that never enter the mode (mintty, GitBash) therefore keep the classic VT path: a lone `Esc` keeps its normal response time, and a letter typed after a timed-out `ESC[` is not swallowed.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：Incomplete records are held for a bounded recovery window (1 second from first capture, never extended by later input; 64 bytes max); past either bound the hold ends and input is handled as before. Unrecognized complete CSI sequences are not inserted as text; after a damaged CSI prefix, a bare ASCII letter can be consumed as its terminator, while normal Win32 key records and bracketed-paste text retain their own boundaries.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：A session's very first record can still leave residue if it is split before its record-specific shape forms; once any record has been decoded, every split position is covered. Inside the recovery window, literal input starting with `[digit;…` cannot be told apart from a protocol prefix — it may be held, or re-joined to a preceding `Esc`. To type it, wait for the window to close, or avoid that shape right after `Esc`.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：Terminal replies that arrive split are reassembled the same way (native Windows ConPTY is the common source): while the app still has a query awaiting its answer, an unfinished DA1 / DA2 / DSR / DECRPM / XTVERSION tail — even one split again after the introducer `Esc` was flushed — is held across input delays, but only while its shape can still complete into the response type that query expects. It is then consumed as the reply it completes instead of entering the prompt as protocol text.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：That claim is evidence-gated, and this is the difference from earlier builds: no query awaiting an answer means nothing is claimed, so a literal `[?61;4c` typed right after `Esc` still enters the prompt exactly as before.

The window is bounded like the record hold (about a second, never extended by later input; 64 bytes max); past either bound it ends, and bytes still shaped like an unfinished reply prefix are dropped rather than shown.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：Inside that window, with a query of the matching response type outstanding, same-shaped literal input can still be claimed as a reply; to type it, wait for the window to close (about a second), or avoid that shape while a query is outstanding.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：Fragmented SGR mouse reports no longer land in the prompt as text: an incomplete report header is held until the rest arrives, and a report that completes is handled as a mouse event. The hold is armed only while mouse reporting is actually active (fullscreen, with mouse tracking enabled); inline sessions and terminals that never enable tracking keep the existing behavior. The claim window is bounded from first capture (at most 1 second; 64 bytes max), and a continuation arriving inside it is still claimed rather than replayed. Release has no timer: once a parse call sees either bound exceeded, it replays the held bytes as ordinary keys in arrival order — literal input can be delayed, but is never dropped.
A completed text-only assistant reply containing only a leading `⏵` status line remains visible in the conversation and can be selected for copying. Live status lines and status lines followed by a real answer stay out of the transcript body.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：Plugin slash-command results, including errors, remain as local transcript blocks for scrolling and copying during the current session. Indentation and line breaks are preserved. Each report retains at most 200 lines, 65,536 UTF-16 code units and 4,000 terminal cells per line, plus a visible truncation marker. The local display rows are not sent as model input or replayed as conversation history. The backend may separately persist command audit events and their results. Older local report blocks are evicted within the shared 600-row budget. Explicit built-in report layouts (such as `/goal`) keep their existing formatting.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：Mouse (fullscreen): drag to select and copy, double/triple click to select a word or line, click tool cards, timeline ticks and `[Image #N]` previews.

Automatic copies keep the text selected; press `Esc` to clear it or start a new selection to replace it. Selection highlighting skips trailing padding and blank rows while preserving spaces within text and code indentation. Inline mode uses the terminal's native selection.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：When a fullscreen selection starts in a code block's body, soft-wrapped rows join without adding frame padding or newlines, in both light and full frames. Hard line breaks and the existing hard-line inset remain part of screen copying.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：During a fullscreen text drag, the native cursor follows the selected text's edge using your terminal's enabled cursor animation or trail effects. Moving into trailing padding or blank rows keeps it at the nearest selected text edge. Releasing or cancelling the drag restores the focused input's caret.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：File paths in prose can open the file-action menu; automatic detection does not extract a path from inside a slash-delimited token such as `working/idle/needs-input` or a date such as `2024/01/15`.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：**Pasting**: the launchpad accepts clipboard images and pasted image paths as `[Image #N]` attachments; `Enter` sends them with the first message. Commands that do not accept images preserve the draft and its attachments. Image chips behave like chat: arrows step across them, Backspace at the end or Delete at the start removes the whole image, and Ctrl+W never splits a chip. Text pasted on the launchpad is folded to one line. In chat, native and bracketed paste keeps ordinary text and newlines, and never submits itself on arrival. On Windows terminals that deliver a paste as win32-input-mode key records, a record stream leaked into the payload is decoded back into the characters its `Uc` field encodes — newlines included — so the composer's line count matches what was pasted; only records with no character meaning are stripped (a multi-line paste no longer leaves stray `_`), and a complete record is always consumed before an ESC-less tail, so no payload character is deleted along with an orphan escape. Pasted CRLF collapses to a single newline; genuine underscores and bracketed-paste text are untouched.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：**Dropped files**: a native Windows desktop drop (Windows Terminal / OpenConsole) arrives as an OSC 8 hyperlink; the parser restores its `file://` URI to a decoded local path before paste hygiene runs, so the `]8;id=…;` parameter bytes never reach the draft. Image paths enter the existing image staging pipeline; other files are inserted as a referenceable path (a path containing whitespace arrives in the composer's quoted `"…"` single-token form). Only `file://` URIs are restored, and it is fail-closed: a remote authority/UNC, a payload carrying several distinct URIs, or a URI that carries several tokens is refused and stays literal text rather than guessed.
Fullscreen drag-copy uses the final highlight. If a live row changed during a drag,
move the selection back to stable text to establish a new baseline. A stationary
selection whose copied text changes is still refused; automatic scroll/resize
does not clear that protection.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：The pixel whale, large title and context/TPS colors follow the same terminal color depth as other text: monochrome, 16-color, 256-color or truecolor. Apple Terminal and tmux use the shared fallback; `NO_COLOR` and `FORCE_COLOR` retain the existing shared color policy.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Keybindings & Mouse：If resume reports that another DSH process owns the writer, release the session in that process (for example, dsh web) and retry in the same TUI. @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Known Limitations：- Shutdown drains only the actual renderer-owned input after terminal cleanup and a 150-ms settle window. Embedders retaining only `unmount` keep that input lease; wrappers replacing the method must pass the renderer’s `shutdownInput` lease to `finishExit`. Custom input drains its own buffered bytes; a device-specific kernel drain can be supplied as the bounded synchronous `render({ drainStdin })` callback. Revoked/replaced owners and non-TTY input are not drained. The window does not guarantee arbitrary SSH latency.
- Local Windows copying uses PowerShell with UTF-8 stdin. Copies run in order; each PowerShell attempt has a two-second timeout (Windows PowerShell, then PowerShell 7). If both fail, OSC 52 remains the fallback and requires terminal support. SSH never writes the remote native clipboard.
- Catchable exits explicitly end synchronized output (DEC 2026) as part of terminal cleanup, even without a final frame. SIGKILL, native aborts and a fully blocked JavaScript event loop cannot guarantee in-process cleanup; recovery then requires the terminal or an external supervisor.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Plugin Ecosystem：Typing `/plugin install ` lists these three shapes in the completion popup, and the same shapes follow the installed names on `/plugin info `. @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Plugin Ecosystem：Managing what is installed: `/plugin remove <bundle>`, `/plugin enable <name | row id>` and `/plugin disable <name | row id>`. A bundle is a composition layer and a row is one patch entry, so the two are separate actions, and a bundle name is matched before any row identity. A module name shared by multiple rows requires a specific row ID. **Gate 2 refuses the three ways this app could switch itself off** — removing or disabling the bundle that provides it, the host layer `dsh-base`, or one of its own rows — and says which rule it broke, without calling the service at all; that holds whether or not hot reload is live, which is the path the host's own guard misses. `enable` is never refused by gate 2 (it is the repair action). Every enable and removal asks first; `disable` asks only about a host-layer row. The host does not attest installed package sources, so even an exact feed match requires confirmation before enabling.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Plugin Ecosystem：These three actions have no cancellation — the service offers none — so `esc` only closes the pane while the write finishes and reports itself into the transcript. Enable and disable have no CLI verb either (the service writes them into the profile's own files). **Grants follow the lifecycle**: `enable` enables and grants the declared permissions, `disable` disables and revokes the permissions that component declared, and `remove` **deletes the component's `grants`/`denies` entries** after the removal — grants are keyed by component id, so leaving them behind lets any later package reusing that id inherit them silently; a reinstall asks again. Backend data directories, storage namespaces and the effect ledger stay, and the residue report names each source by its path. A failed grant write never blocks an install or enable — it is reported instead. Grants are behavioural constraints, not a security boundary.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Plugin Ecosystem：`/plugin list` also advertises the experimental features DSH ships, leaves off by default, and this app knows how to drive (currently Agent Teams, Auto review, Session search and Git worktrees), each with its switch and usage line. A DSH installation that does not ship one shows no such section.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Permissions and Security Boundary：> **Windows security warning:** the Windows profile defaults to `danger-full-access` with approval set to `never`, so tools have unrestricted access. Inspect and tighten the profile before starting next to sensitive credentials or in an untrusted repository.

No sandbox of its own: dsh-TUI uses the active DSH profile's filesystem, shell, sandbox and approval policies. Permission presets come from the DSH `permissionPresets` registry.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Permissions and Security Boundary：**Permission persistence** (all three backends): the Claude and Codex backends keep their `/permission` picks in `~/.dsh-tui/backends/<id>/prefs.json`; the DSH pick is kept at `~/.dsh-tui/permission.json`. Every durable preset switch teaches it (picker, typed `/permission`, Shift+Tab static modes, or a switch the official command performed on its own), and a session that never customized its permission planes starts on the remembered preset — applied through the same official switch path. "Never customized" is about the user: the composition writes its own default preset into every fresh session at creation, and those events do not count. Plan-mode transients and the experimental Auto review preset (see below) are excluded, a `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` launch pin (this run's initial permission plane) outranks the file, and an identity the mounted roster no longer offers is skipped.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Permissions and Security Boundary：**Auto review** (DSH, experimental): `/plugin list` advertises it; after `/plugin enable @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-auto-review`, the `auto` preset (shown as "Auto review", tagged `EXP`) appears in `/permission` and its completions live, and disappears when the plugin is removed. It is session-only: the model reviews every tool call before it runs, there is no file sandbox, and each call costs one extra model request; its approval prompts show the localized reason, and a subagent denial reads "Auto review denied; not executed". Picking it in the picker first shows a risk confirmation (`Enter` enables, `Esc` goes back; in fullscreen its Enable / Go back rows are clickable); a typed `/permission auto` switches directly. Once the current session has selected it, the picker skips the confirmation and Shift+Tab stops skipping it.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Permissions and Security Boundary：**Session search** (DSH, experimental): `/plugin list` advertises it; after `/plugin enable @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-session-search`, an agent gains five read-only tools (`session_search`, `session_event_search`, `session_trace`, `session_event_trace`, `session_event_read`) over earlier sessions in the same workspace — cross-session access requires an identical `cwd`. The index is in memory and is built on the first search; nothing is written to disk. This app keeps the kernel Minimal preset at its single persistent-shell tool, so Minimal never shows these five tools or their usage guidance.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Permissions and Security Boundary：**Git worktrees** (DSH, experimental): `/plugin list` advertises it; after `/plugin enable @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-tool-worktree`, an agent gains `create_worktree`, which creates a new Git branch and a checkout under `.agents/worktrees/<name>` of the current repository (from `HEAD` or a local revision; uncommitted files stay in the source checkout) and moves the session into it — the status line, Git branch and `@` completion follow, while the session stays registered under its project. Its card reads `Worktree("<branch>")` with the checkout path and base revision. Nothing is cleaned up: remove the checkout with `git worktree remove <path>` and the branch separately with `git branch -D <branch>` (the agent leaves with `working_directory`; once the checkout is gone, the next request returns the session to the project). A leftover branch makes a later `create_worktree` with the same name fail. Calling it from inside a worktree nests the new checkout under that worktree. @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Permissions and Security Boundary：**Upstream auto-retry** (DSH): whenever a session binds (boot, `/model` switch, resume), the TUI seeds a retry policy — 5 attempts, transport-drop-aware failure codes including `STREAM_CLOSED` (a dropped upstream stream) — on **the provider route that session actually uses**, through the official `llm-pi-ai` settings section (the policy the kernel's `llm-retry` plugin executes). Only routes without an explicit `retryPolicy` are seeded — dormant channels are never written — and `upstreamRetry: false` in cordis.yml opts out.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Storage migration and read budgets：The SQLite migration script uses the official `node:sqlite.backup()` API on
supported Node 22.19+ and Node 24+ builds. It probes that capability before
opening the source read-only and includes committed WAL data in a consistent
snapshot; it never copies a live database/WAL pair by hand. A build missing the
API reports a migration-specific prerequisite. Session-tree reads validate packed
rows and check their entire member count against the remaining scan budget before
expanding events. Oversized rows report truncation; malformed rows report failure.
The logical budget does not eliminate physical JSON/frame parsing or validation.
Development `@deepseek-ai/*` release-age exceptions list only exact package versions in the current
lockfile (including the legacy SQLite island); all other versions retain the
24-hour delay. Regenerate with `node scripts/verify-release-age-cohort.mjs --write`
after an intentional lockfile update, then review the cohort diff.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Bounded update installation：`/update` and `dsh-tui update` give each installer invocation (profile and engine) a **30-minute
wall-clock limit**. Set `DSH_TUI_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS` to a positive integer in
milliseconds to change it (invalid values use the default). Output activity does
not reset this deadline; a quiet but healthy installation can use the full limit.
Only the final process exit code establishes success: a printed `Done` does not.
Ctrl+C cancels the owned installer. On POSIX, cancellation terminates its own
process group, then force-kills remaining descendants after two seconds. Windows
uses a dedicated PowerShell/native supervisor with a private Job Object. The
installer joins that job atomically while suspended; verified membership is required
before it runs. The supervisor retains the job handle after the root exits, so
cancellation and timeout also terminate orphaned descendants holding output pipes.
It does not enable job breakaway or kill processes by name or an exited root PID.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Bounded update installation：Windows requires Windows 10 / Server 2016 or later and Windows PowerShell with
`Add-Type`/native interop available. Startup or job-membership failures stop the
installation before running an unowned installer. A cleanup failure is reported as
unconfirmed, never as proof that all writes stopped. Timeout, cancellation, or
unconfirmed cleanup returns nonzero and prevents retries, stale-file removal,
repair, and TUI replacement. A partial installation may remain: check/repair that
profile before using the recovery command printed at update start and on failure.
`~/.dsh-tui/restart.log` records installer category, PID, termination reason and last
output timestamp before any restart.

@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui README · Bounded update installation：The focused **Windows installer process ownership** workflow runs the real native
regression on `windows-latest`, with Node 24 and no dependency installation. To run
it locally on Windows: `node scripts/verify-update-process-windows.mjs`. It checks
orphan descendants, timeout/cancellation, nested jobs, failure diagnostics, streams,
arguments and an unrelated process; a Linux run explicitly skips native acceptance.
